paragraphs: Bekol yemot hachol nishlamim mea berakot etzel kol adam "y birkot hashshachar ubirkot hattepilla mittechilla vead sop, v"y berakot shel akila ushetiyya, ubeshabbat veyom tob asher yechsar lo min birkot haamida yashlim bemine perot ubesamim, ubeyom hattaanit yechsar lo harbeh berakot ubiprat keshemmitanneh layla veyom sheen akila ushetiyya ballayla ubayyom, yizzaher lishmoa birkot haqqorein battora veoneh acharehem amen vezeh yoil lehashlim bishat haddechaq heka dela epshar, mihu tzarik sheyyishma kol habberaka mittechilla vead sop:

clarification.explanation: On every weekday a person completes a hundred berachot through the morning blessings, the blessings of the prayer service from its beginning to its end, and the blessings over eating and drinking. On Shabbat and Yom Tov, where blessings are lacking from the (shortened) Amidah prayer, one completes the count with [blessings over] various fruits and spices. On a fast day — especially a fast lasting a full night and day without eating or drinking — many blessings are lacking, and so it is fitting to listen to the blessings of those called up to the Torah and answer Amen, which helps complete the count in a time of difficulty; but one must hear the entire blessing from beginning to end.
takeaways: Every day one completes a hundred berachot (on Shabbat/Yom Tov — with blessings over fruits and spices).
On a fast day, listening to the Torah-reading blessings and answering Amen helps complete the count.

paragraphs: Hambarek tzarik lehashmia leazenayv habberaka, veyizzaher lebarek bemittun bekavvanot halleb keotam burim hambarekim bedillug otiyyot vetebot, veim dilleg shem o malkut yachazor vibarek, dekol beraka sheen bah shem umalkut enah beraka, vaapillu lo yedalleg ella tebat haolam lebad yachazor vibarek ki melek lebad enah malkut:

clarification.explanation: One who recites a berachah must make it audible to his own ears, and must bless slowly and with intention of the heart — not by skipping letters and words as the masses do. If he skipped God's Name or 'Kingship' (King of the world) he must go back and bless again, for a berachah without Name and Kingship is not a berachah at all; and even if he skipped only the word 'ha'olam' (the world), he must go back, because 'King' alone is not 'Kingship'.
takeaways: A berachah must contain God's Name and 'Kingship' (including the word 'ha'olam') in full — any omission requires repeating the berachah.

paragraphs: Tzarik lehizzaher shello yapsiq ben beraka laakila o shetiyya yoter mikkede dibbur dehaynu kede amirat shalom aleka rabbi shehu shelosh tebot, remez laddabar (mishle kd, z): "bashshaar lo yiptach pihu" bsh"r rashe tebot beshiur shalom aleka rabbi, mihu bibtzia shel hammotzi kesheokel im acherim hittiru libtzoa perusa gedola kede litten mimmenna lamsubbin v"p sh"y batzeu perusa gedola shoheh yoter mikkede dibbur huttar lo zeh mishshum mitzva, veal kol panim yizzaher leekol meotah happerusa qodem sheyyibtza mimmenna lamsubbin, veal ken im ba lishtot mayim verotzeh lishpok mehem qetzat yishpok qodem sheyyebarek kede lemaher lishtot achar beraka, ubazeh yesh od taam acher shello lishpok achar habberaka mippene habbizzayon shel habberaka shechala kebar al kol hammayim shebbakkeli ukemo shekkatab rabbenu zalman za"l, veken yesh lizzaher kesheshshoteh mashqeh cham shello yenopep bispatayv leqoreru achar habberaka ella yaaseh qodem, veyesh lizzaher shello yebarek al maakol umashqeh cham beyoter, mishshum dechosheshin shemma yishheh mippene hachom veayyen chesed laalapim:

clarification.explanation: One must not pause between the berachah and the eating/drinking for longer than 'the time it takes to speak' (the time needed to say 'Shalom alekha Rabbi' — three words). In cutting the 'HaMotzi' bread when eating with others, it was permitted to cut a large slice in order to give some to those at the table (even though this takes longer than the permitted pause, because it serves a mitzvah), but one should taste from the slice before giving from it to the others. Therefore, one who is about to drink water and wants to pour out some of it should pour it out before the berachah; and likewise one should not purse the lips to cool a hot drink after the berachah, but rather beforehand.
takeaways: One may not pause between the berachah and eating for longer than 'the time it takes to speak' (except for cutting bread for others at the table — permitted, though one should taste it first).
Preparations such as pouring off excess water or cooling a hot drink are done before the berachah, not after.

paragraphs: Im libbo roeh et haerva sheen lo ezor o kesut dachuq asur lebarek, veken rosho megulleh asur lebarek, vekol dabar shemmebarek alayv yochazennu beyamin, ubeseper chasidim katab im moshitin lo seper tzarik sheyyiqqachennu beyad yamin veen litchob happeri shemmebarek alayv besakkin veyochazenna bimino, ki hem shene hapkiyyim dehayyamin mimmennu totzaot chayyim vehassakkin meqatztzer veayyen eshel abraham verabbenu zalman za"l vetzarik lehizzaher shehammazleg yihyeh shel kesep velo shel barzel, ki yesh dabar demukrach litchob bemazleg ulebarek:

clarification.explanation: One whose nakedness would be visible to his own eye — because he has no belt and no snug-fitting garment — may not recite a berachah, and likewise one with an uncovered head may not recite a berachah. What one blesses over should be held in the right hand. One should not skewer fruit with a knife in order to bless it while holding it in the right hand, since the right hand symbolizes life while the knife shortens life — two opposites; but if a fork is needed, it should be of silver rather than iron.
takeaways: One may not recite a berachah while one's nakedness is exposed or the head is uncovered; hold what is being blessed in the right hand.
Avoid a knife (which shortens) when blessing over fruit; a silver fork is preferable to an iron one.

paragraphs: Haomed al ammat hammayim mebarek veshoteh meammat hammayim, "p shehammayim shehayu lepanayv beet habberaka chillepu veholeko, mippene sheddato haya al mayim sheyyabo besiyyum birkato vaalehem chala habberaka, velo od ella apillu im natal beyado peri min hakkeli sheyyesh bo perot uberak alayv, ubesiyyum habberaka napal miyyado veneebad o nimas yiqqach peri acher mehakkeli veyokal al semak otah beraka mippene sheddato haya leekol gam ken min happerot shebbakkeli ulekak chala alehem habberaka, v"g deyesh choleqin bedin zeh shel happeri shennapal im kol zeh sapeq berakot lehaqel velo yebarek od, vehaynu davqa shehaya bedato beet habberaka leekol od mimmah shilpenu "p im lo haya nopel happeri miyyado, vehu haddin im berak al kos yayin venishpak vehaya qanqan yayin munnach lepanayv vehaya bedato lishtot od mimmennu, abal im lo haya bedato ella leekol oto happeri shehaya beyado davqa, velo lishtot ella oto hakkos shehaya beyado, hinneh atta shenneebad o nishpak nimtzet birkato lebattala veomer "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed", veim yirtzeh leekol perot min hakkelali tzarik lachazor ulebarek, mihu gam bazeh yishtaddel lehabi adam acher sheyyebarek al happeri vikavven alayv, o yabi peri min acher shebbirkato shava im oto happeri vibarek alayv, vekol zeh im siyyem habberaka sheamar tebat "elohenu" gam ken, abal im lo amar ella "baruk atta Adonai" venapal happeri o hakkos miyyado yesayyem lammedeni chuqqeka denireh keqore pasuq tehillim, veaz yiqqach peri acher vibarek alayv:

clarification.explanation: One standing beside a water channel who blesses over the water in order to drink — even though the water that was before him at the time of the berachah has already flowed past — may drink from the water that comes afterward, because his intent was on that water. Likewise, if he blessed over a fruit and it fell from his hand before he ate it, he may take another fruit from the same vessel and eat it relying on the berachah, because his intent was to eat from those [fruits generally]. This applies specifically when he intended from the start to eat more from the vessel; but if he intended only that specific fruit/cup and it was lost — his berachah was in vain (he says 'Barukh shem kevod malkhuto le'olam va'ed'), and if he wants to eat more he must bless again (or have someone else bless with intent to include him). All of this applies once he had already said the word 'Eloheinu' in his berachah; but if he had said only 'Barukh atah Hashem' and the fruit or cup fell from his hand before he completed the berachah, he should finish with 'Lamdeni chukekha' (Psalms 119:12), so that it appears as a verse of Psalms rather than an interrupted berachah, and then take another fruit and bless over it.
takeaways: A berachah intended also to cover additional water/fruit from the same source covers them even if the first is lost.
A berachah intended only for one specific item that was lost is in vain, and a new berachah is required (or another person blesses on his behalf).

paragraphs: Im natal peri beyado ubarek alayv veraa acher yapeh mimmennu lo yachalipennu, "p shebbedato haya beet shebberak gam al zeh happeri haacher:

clarification.explanation: One who took a fruit in hand and blessed over it, and then saw a nicer fruit — should not switch to it, even though at the time of the berachah he had intended to include that other fruit as well.
takeaways: One may not switch to a nicer fruit after already having blessed over the first one, even if he had intended it in advance.

paragraphs: Haya okel perot derek aray vehebiu lo od, im haya dato mittechilla al mah sheyyabiu lo eno chozer umebarek al mah shehebiu lo "p shekkebar akal kol mah shehaya lepanayv, veim lo haya dato mittechilla ella raq leekol et ellu happerot shellepanayv davqa venimlak leekol od veamar sheyyabiu lo tzarik lebarek al mah sheyyabiu lo, apillu yesh adayin lepanayv min happeri, veim hu bistam hinneh kol zeman shemmunnach lepanayv min happeri shekkebar berak alayv yesh pelugetta bedabar zeh deyesh omerim tzarik lebarek veyesh omerim en tzarik lebarek umeachar deqayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel lo yebarek mihu "g dekatebu happoseqim deamerinan sapeq berakot lehaqel apillu bequm ekol veayyen chesed laalapim siman r"v bimchuddash ot Adonai yeuyyan sham, mikkol maqom bequm ekol kol heka deepshar lanu letaqqen metaqqeninan vehu sheyyebarek al meat sukkar shehakkol veyiptor gam oto happeri, o yabo adam acher vibarek veyokal vikavven alayv, veim i epshar bekol opannim ellu yebarek beli shem umalkut, veraq yeharher shem umalkut belibbo: vekol zeh im hu bistam, veyesh adayin lepanayv meoto happeri shebberak alayv kebar, ubehay gavna hu deikka pelugta hannizkeret leel: abal im hu bistam, veakal kol mah shehaya lepanayv, veaach"k hebiu lo - hare zeh mebarek lekulle alema al mah shehebiu lo, mippene shehu haya okel bederek aray. veen chilluq ben im hebiu lo mimmin harishon o mimmin haacher shebbirkato shava im harishon. veim qaba atzmo al hashshulchan laakilat perot, az apillu im akal kol mah shehaya lepanayv, veaach"k hebiu lo od - en tzarik lebarek, dekol sheqqaba atzmo laakilat perot eno massicha dato kol zeman shemmeseb al hashshulchan. vegam bazeh en chilluq ben hebiu lo mimmin harishon o mimmin shebbirkato shava.

clarification.explanation: One who ate fruit casually (without formally establishing himself for it) and more was brought to him: if from the start his intent had covered also what would be brought, he need not bless again on the addition, even though he had already finished what was before him. If from the start he intended only the fruit before him, and then reconsidered and asked for more — he must bless on what was brought, even if some of the first fruit remains. If he ate with no specific intent either way, then as long as some of the fruit he already blessed over remains before him, there is a dispute: some say he must bless on the addition, some say not; and since a doubt about berachot is resolved leniently, he should not bless. But since the doubt can be remedied, it is preferable: he should bless 'shehakol' over a bit of sugar and thereby discharge the fruit as well, or have another person bless and eat with intent to include him; and if neither is possible, he should bless without uttering God's Name and Kingship, merely contemplating them in his heart. All this dispute applies specifically when he ate without specific intent and some of the first fruit still remains before him. But if he ate without specific intent and finished everything before him, and only then was more brought — he blesses on the addition according to all opinions, since he ate casually; and it makes no difference whether what was brought is the same kind or another kind with the same berachah. And if he had established himself at the table for eating fruit — then even having finished everything before him and having more brought, he does not bless again, since one who has established himself does not lose his intent as long as he remains seated at the table; and here too there is no difference between the same kind and a kind with the same berachah.
takeaways: Intent covering the addition in advance — no new berachah; reconsidering and asking for more — a new berachah is required, even if some of the original remains.
Eating with no specific intent while some of the original fruit remains — doubtful, so no new berachah (best resolved via a 'shehakol' over sugar).
Finishing everything eaten casually and then having more brought — bless according to all opinions; having established oneself for the meal — no new berachah.

paragraphs: Apillu im qaba laakilat perot, im siyyem akilato vesilleqo happerot millepanayv, vegamar bedato lebarek beraka acharona, ak lo berak beraka acharona ad sheabar zeman mah mippene shennitasseq bedabar acher, veaach"k matza meoto hammin peri shennapal al hammitta o beqeren zavit o al haaretz - hare zeh nimlak bevadday, vetzarik lebarek al oto happeri shemmatza im yirtzeh leakelo. mihu yoter tob limnoa atzmo mizzeh shello leekol kede shello yebarek.

clarification.explanation: One who established himself for eating fruit, finished, and the fruit was cleared away, and he had resolved to recite the closing berachah but had not yet done so because he became occupied with something else in the meantime — if he then found, of that same kind, [a piece] that had fallen (on the bed, in a corner, or on the floor), this is regarded as having 'reconsidered,' and he must bless if he wants to eat it. It is preferable to refrain from eating it so as to avoid the doubt of a berachah.
takeaways: Fruit found after a fruit-meal has ended (that had fallen earlier) has the status of 'reconsidering' — one blesses over it if he wishes to eat it.

paragraphs: Im achar shebberak al mah shellepanayv veakal mimmennu hebiu lo peri min acher shebbirkato shava, ak hu chashub vechabib alayv yoter mimmin harishon shehaya lepanayv - tzarik lebarek al hechadash, im lo haya bedato lepatero bibraka shel harishon beperush, sheeno baddin sheyyiptor peri sheeno chashub lapperi hechashub lechabib derek garera ella im ken nitkavven bedato lepatero,veayyen "chayye-adam", kelal s, avvat b. vekol zeh la mayre ella beadam haokel mishshello, abal okel al shulchan acherim kevan shebberak al min echad poter kol mah sheyyabiu lo od apillu lo haya lepanayv od min harishonot, dehakkol taluy bedaat baal habbayit, im lo shennimlak mammash, vekol shehu okel al shulchan baal habbayit apillu lo haya bedaat baal habbayit litten laorechim yoter mimmah sheyyesh lipnehem raq lebaqqashat haorechim natan lahem od, apillu hake en tzerikim lachazor ulebarek mishshum deattakka debaal habbayit somekin sheyyodein sheyyittenu lahem kol tzarekam veen osin hessach haddaat veayyen chayye adam kelal s' ot Adonai:

clarification.explanation: If, after blessing and eating, another fruit of the same berachah is brought that is more important and dearer to him than the first — he must bless again on it, unless he had explicitly intended to discharge it as well with the first berachah (one does not discharge something important via something less important incidentally). This applies to one eating his own food; but one eating at another's table — his berachah on one kind discharges everything else brought to him, since it all depends on the host's intent (unless he truly reconsidered).
takeaways: A more important fruit brought after the berachah requires a new berachah, unless it was intended in advance.
One eating at a host's table is discharged by whatever is brought, since he relies on the host's intent.

paragraphs: Oreach hanniknas lebet chabero vehebiu lo kos mashqeh sukkar shebbirkato shehakkol, veaach"k hebiu lo mashqeh qhvv" (qapeh) debirkato shehakkol lo yebarek al qhvv" deniptar bibraka rishona mippene ki yesh bene adam shemmekabbedin laoreach bemashqeh shel qhvv" bilbad veyesh shemmekabbedin bazeh ubazeh, mihu tob shehaoreach yekavven bammashqeh harishon sheyyabiu lo liptor gam mashqeh haacher sheyyoshitu lo aach"k, vehaadam yaaseh mizzeh haqqash lekamma dabar dirgili behu inashe bammaqom hahu:

clarification.explanation: A guest given a cup of sugar-water (berachah 'shehakol') and afterward coffee (also 'shehakol') does not bless on the coffee, since it is discharged by the first berachah; and it is good for the guest to intend, with the first drink, to discharge also what will be handed to him afterward.
takeaways: Drinks sharing the same berachah served one after another to a guest — the first discharges those that follow.

paragraphs: Laqach dabar shebbirkato "bore peri haadama" vechashab shehu peri haetz, uberak addata deetz sheamar "baruk atta Adonai elohenu melek haolam" al daat lomar haetz venizkar vesiyyem "bore peri haadama" yatza, veken hu haddin im laqach dabar shebbirkato shehakkol vechashab shehu etz upatach uberak al daat lomar haetz venizkar veamar "shehakkol" yatza, veken hu haddin im laqach kos mashqeh shebbirkato "shehakkol" vesabur shehu yayin gam ken dina haki deyatza, ak ledaat haramba"m za"l lo yatza kevan dibiqqar habberaka haya bedato lomar shello kahogen, ketzad yaaseh mishshum sapeq berakot yitom mah shebbeyado shebberek alayv kede shello tihyeh birkato lebattala lekulle alema, umishshum chashashat sabar haramba"m za"l yitten laacherim sheyyebareku veyoklu mimmennu vikavvenu lepatero veaz yokal kirtzono: umihu im zeh happeri shehaya beyado birkato "bore peri haetz" vechashab shehu peri adama, veamar "baruk atta Adonai elohenu melek haolam" al daat lomar "bore peri haadama" venizkar vesiyyem "bore peri haetz" yatza lekulle alema veen tzarik letaqqen bazeh, yaan sheim berak al dabar shebbirkato "etz" "bore peri haadama" yatza, veken hu haddin im zeh birkat etz o "bore peri haggapen" vechashab shebbirkato "shehakkol" upatach lomar shehakkol vesiyyem birkato haiqqarit yatza lekulle alema, mishshum deal hakkol im berak "shehakkol" yatza:

clarification.explanation: One who took something whose berachah is 'borei pri ha'adamah,' thinking it was a tree-fruit, and began to bless with 'ha'etz' in mind, but then remembered and concluded 'borei pri ha'adamah' — he has fulfilled his obligation. The same applies to a similar mix-up between 'shehakol' and 'ha'etz' or 'wine' — he has fulfilled his obligation (though according to the Rambam one should be stringent, and so it is good to taste it and resolve the doubt by having another person bless and intend to discharge him). But if his true berachah was 'ha'etz' and he thought it was 'ha'adamah,' and he began with 'ha'adamah' but then remembered and concluded 'ha'etz' — he has fulfilled his obligation according to all opinions with no need for remedy, since the berachah 'ha'adamah' is effective even for a tree-fruit.
takeaways: A mix-up between berachah formulas, corrected before finishing, fulfills the obligation in most cases.
'Ha'adamah' over a tree-fruit is effective by the letter of the law; the reverse (ha'etz over ha'adamah) is more doubtful, so it is best to remedy it.

paragraphs: Im berak al peri adama "bore peri haetz" vetok kede dibbur nizkar shettaa veamar "bore peri haadama", vekak hayeta birkato "baruk atta Adonai elohenu melek haolam bore peri haetz, bore peri haadama" yatza, v"g deyesh choleqin qayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel, veken hu haddin betaa bedabar shebbirkato "shehakkol" uberak "etz" o mashqeh shebbirkato "shehakkol" uberak "bore peri haggapen":

clarification.explanation: One who blessed over a ground-fruit 'borei pri ha'etz,' and immediately, within the time it takes to speak, remembered and concluded 'borei pri ha'adamah' (so that the berachah as spoken was '...borei pri ha'etz, borei pri ha'adamah') — he has fulfilled his obligation (even though some disagree, a doubt about berachot is resolved leniently). The same applies to a similar mix-up between 'shehakol' and 'ha'etz' or 'wine'.
takeaways: An immediate correction (within the time it takes to speak) of a mistaken berachah is effective and fulfills the obligation.

paragraphs: Taa uberak al hallechem "bore mine mezonot" - yatza, vaapillu shear mine maakol umashqeh, im taa uberak alehem "bore mine mezonot" - yatza, debilshon tora hakkol niqra "mazon", chutz mimmayim umelach, velaken im taa uberak al hammayim "bore mine mezonot" - lo yatza, vetzarik lomar "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed", veyachazor vibarek al hammayim "shehakkol nihya bidbaro", vekannizkar b"chayye adam", kelal nch, avvat g. vekol dine tauyot hannizkarim leel shekkatabnu deyotze yede chobato, haynu raq bediabad, abal lekattechilla qodem sheyyebarek tzarik sheyyeda vikavven habberaka shetztzarik lebarek, kede shebbehazkarat hashshem - shehu iqqar habberaka - yihyeh yodea mah shemmesayyem baamittut, vetabo alayv beraka.

clarification.explanation: One who erred and blessed 'borei minei mezonot' over bread, or over other foods and drinks, has fulfilled his obligation, since in the language of the Torah everything is called 'mazon' (sustenance), except for water and salt. Therefore, one who erred and blessed 'minei mezonot' over water has not fulfilled his obligation, and must say 'Barukh shem kevod malkhuto le'olam va'ed' and go back and bless 'shehakol nihyeh bidvaro.' All the laws of error stated above apply only after the fact — but ideally, one must know and intend the correct berachah in advance.
takeaways: 'Borei minei mezonot' after the fact discharges the obligation as a general berachah (except for water and salt) — but ideally one must bless precisely.
